3: The patient presents with a large submucosal bulging mass in the posterior gastric wall with ulcerated areas, and imaging studies show a well-defined, homogeneous, oval mass with fat-tissue attenuation and central contrast enhancement, which is consistent with a GIST.
The mass has fat-tissue attenuation on CT, which could be consistent with a lipoma, although the presence of ulcerated areas and the large size of the mass make GIST more likely.
